prompts.text: What was your favourite way to spend time with friends after school?
Tell me about a friendship that began because you both liked the same unusual activity.
Revisit a childhood friend's old neighbourhood or look through memories of a school event together?
You could arrange a reunion of the children who played on your street. What activity would help everyone reconnect?
Childhood friendships can feel effortless because people meet simply by going outside.
The childhood friends people remember most aren't always the ones they spent the most time with.
Which small kindness from a childhood friend do you still remember?
Recall sharing a secret project or game with a friend when you were young.
You're showing your old best friend a picture from school days. What story would the picture bring up?
Share a memory of a first friend or hear somebody else's story about meeting theirs?
What was the most interesting thing you ever collected as a child?
Describe finding an object that became more valuable to you because of where you discovered it.
Keep a box of childhood treasures or take photographs of them before giving some away?
A school asks you to create an exhibit of ordinary childhood collections. What would you display?
Small collections often show how children make sense of the world around them.
A collection doesn't have to be rare or expensive to hold an interesting story.
Which childhood possession did you protect with surprising seriousness?
Recall trading or swapping something with a classmate and feeling very grown-up.
You find an old tin of forgotten belongings. Which item would you hope is still there?
Revisit a childhood toy collection or examine the notebooks where you kept little discoveries?
What was your favourite seasonal activity when you were a child?
Tell me about a holiday when the weather changed your plans in an unexpected way.
A long afternoon playing outside or a rainy day inventing games indoors?
You can recreate one ordinary day from a school holiday. How would the morning begin?
School breaks can feel endless to children but impossibly short in hindsight.
Children don't need a complicated schedule to enjoy having free time.
Which smell or sound reminds you of a particular school holiday?
Recall visiting relatives during a break and learning a new game from local children.
A younger cousin says they're bored during a holiday. What could you suggest using what is already around?
Tell stories about your longest holiday or compare the activities you enjoyed during shorter breaks?
What's an outdoor place you explored as a child that felt like a secret world?
Describe learning the names of plants or animals from somebody in your neighbourhood.
Search for interesting leaves or observe birds in a quiet spot?
You get to show a child the natural wonders around an ordinary street. What would you point out?
Children often notice tiny changes in the natural world that busy adults walk past.
An afternoon exploring safely outdoors can be as educational as a formal lesson.
Which insect or animal fascinated you before you learnt much about it?
Recall seeing a dramatic sky or unusual cloud formation during a childhood game.
A family wants to begin keeping a nature journal together. What simple observations should it include?
Visit a botanical garden or spend time beside a small pond watching wildlife?
Which childhood creative project are you still quietly proud of?
Tell me about making a gift for someone using materials you found at home.
Draw a picture from memory or build a small object from cardboard and tape?
You have paper, crayons and one afternoon to recreate a childhood art activity. What would you make?
Children often value the making process more than the neatness of a finished project.
A messy drawing can contain a more memorable idea than a technically perfect one.
Which craft did you enjoy even though you weren't especially good at it?
Recall an adult displaying something you made and how it felt.
A younger relative wants you to join a painting activity. How would you make it relaxing for both of you?
Preserve one childhood drawing or recreate it today with your current skills?
What was the first piece of technology you remember being excited to use?
Describe playing with a household device before you fully understood what it was for.
See your first mobile phone again or spend an afternoon with a childhood games console?
You're explaining to a young child how people communicated before smartphones. What everyday example would you use?
Technology from childhood can feel ancient even when it's only a few years old.
Waiting for a favourite programme or game sometimes made it more exciting.
Which childhood gadget would be funniest to demonstrate to someone who has never seen one?
Recall learning to operate a radio, camera or computer with somebody's guidance.
You find an old device containing family pictures but no modern connection. How would you preserve the memories safely?
Revisit a classic game you played on a basic device or explore a museum of older technology?
What made birthdays exciting for you before you cared about elaborate plans?
Tell me about a childhood celebration where a tiny surprise meant more than any gift.
A simple party with neighbourhood friends or a special meal with close family?
You can recreate the atmosphere of a childhood birthday without spending much. What would be essential?
Children often remember who joined a celebration more clearly than the decorations.
A thoughtful birthday tradition can matter more than a large crowd.
Which birthday game or song reminds you most strongly of being young?
Recall a time somebody made you feel special without telling you the plan beforehand.
A family is preparing a low-budget celebration for a child who dislikes loud parties. What would you suggest?
Make a handmade birthday card or organise a favourite childhood game?
What was your most memorable experience of learning to ride or use something new?
Describe the first time you successfully did a task that had seemed impossible a week earlier.
Learn a physical skill through gentle practice or watch someone demonstrate it before you try?
A child is nervous about learning to ride a bicycle. What would make the first session less intimidating?
Children often remember the person who encouraged them as much as the skill they learnt.
Learning slowly is easier when nobody turns every attempt into a competition.
Which childhood achievement made you proud even though it seemed small to adults?
Recall practising a skill so often that you eventually surprised yourself.
Your younger self has just succeeded at something difficult. What would you want an adult to say?
Revisit your first sports skill or remember the first thing you made completely on your own?
What's a school-day sound that you could still recognise instantly?
Tell me about a classroom moment that became funny without anyone intending it.
Remember a favourite school assembly or a class activity that felt unlike a normal lesson?
Your old classroom is reconstructed for a museum visit. Which small detail would make it feel authentic?
School memories can be tied as much to corridors and playgrounds as to particular lessons.
A teacher who made students feel safe to ask questions often taught more than the syllabus.
Which school event encouraged you to discover a new interest?
Recall a classmate who helped you understand something when a lesson felt confusing.
You're invited to talk to students about one enjoyable part of your school days. What story would you tell?
Browse an old yearbook or hear former classmates share memories of a school event?
What childhood memory would you love to hear described by somebody else who was there?
Describe a normal day that became important only after the people involved moved away.
Keep memories as short written stories or record people explaining them in their own voices?
Your family opens a box of shared childhood mementos. How should everyone take turns telling their stories?
Memories become richer when people accept that others noticed different parts of the same event.
Preserving a childhood memory doesn't require pretending that every detail was perfect.
Which positive habit from childhood would you like to continue as an adult?
Recall a simple experience that taught you something you still use today.
A younger person asks what made your childhood enjoyable. How would you answer without idealising the past?
Revisit a place from your past or create a new shared memory inspired by it?
